record.tranche_reason: Tests fitting randomly labeled data with a toy setup and validation accuracy, but uses memory-augmented models and re-initialization rather than the original image-network settings.
record.gate_note: The random-label results are on uniformly generated R8 vectors, not training images. The authors also state that convolutional layers allow ideal fitting, but give no separate measured result for that statement. CIFAR-10, ImageNet, PoseNet, and reconstruction results do not test the claim versions. Figure 4-1 values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Random-label fitting is used to evaluate a proposed product-key memory layer and its re-initialization procedure. The reported comparisons concern a deliberately constructed memory model and a shallow dense replacement, rather than standard deep networks under unchanged training settings. The text also labels the reported accuracy as validation accuracy without establishing that it measures training-set memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report a large effect of re-initialization on their random-label toy benchmark and some image-classification gains. They do not establish standard-network random-label fitting under unchanged settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses uniformly generated R8 vectors with a toy memory-augmented network; the reported near-perfect results rely on multiple memory heads or key re-initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of memory heads and enabling key re-initialization change the reported random-data fitting outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: On 100k uniformly generated eight-dimensional vectors with uniformly random class assignments, the eight-head memory model reportedly fits perfectly; single-head re-initialization gives nearly ideal accuracy, while the dense comparator fails to fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-data memorization by product-key memory models depends on head count and key re-initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 states that convolutional layers permit ideal fitting, but provides no architecture, separate measured result, or training-versus-validation clarification for that observation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A convolutional variant can fit this synthetic random-label benchmark.

record.problems: The random-label experiment uses synthetic vectors rather than images and a nonstandard memory-augmented model. Reported Figure 4-1 outcomes are qualitative in the text, without exact values or uncertainty. No result establishes chance test error or performance on true labels under the same settings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for this claim were reported. Figure 4-2 concerns the re-initialization noise parameter and gives no exact values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Standard deep networks attaining zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Random-versus-real-label training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs with the same networks.
Training fit and test error across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Effects of explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Uniform random vectors are not the Gaussian-noise or pixel-permutation conditions named in V3. Figure 4-2's noise parameter concerns key re-initialization, not input noise or corrupted-label fraction. Its results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test standard deep networks on randomly labeled training images, test error at chance, or unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time for random versus true labels or sweep over corrupted-label fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
No sweep from clean to fully corrupted labels measuring training fit and test error.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or affect true-label generalization.
No measurement of learning order or comparison of real-label and random-label learning over training.

rows.subject: model with no memory
rows.size_stated: Two fully connected projections; 512-dimensional intermediate projection to R15k and back
rows.operation_detail: Trained on randomly labeled data points without a memory block.

conditions.value: 100k uniformly generated vectors in R8; 10 uniformly chosen classes

rows.measure: Top-1 validation accuracy on random-label data
rows.value: The model with no memory is not able to fit the data.
rows.note: The prose describes the no-memory control qualitatively; no exact accuracy is stated.
rows.check: This is the proposed memory method's dense-layer comparator, not an established standard deep-network baseline. Its memory_size condition is inapplicable. The text reports failure to fit qualitatively, but supplies neither training accuracy nor a defined train/validation split; it does not establish absence of V1.

rows.subject: memory model, 8 heads

rows.operation_detail: Trained on randomly labeled data points with an 8-head memory layer.

conditions.value: 100k uniformly generated vectors in R8; 10 uniformly chosen classes

rows.measure: Top-1 validation accuracy on random-label data
rows.value: Full top-1 validation accuracy; the authors describe this as a perfect fit.
rows.note: The described result is for a memory-augmented toy model, not a standard image-classification network.
rows.check: Perfect reported validation accuracy evaluates a custom memory architecture with eight heads and memory capacity matched to dataset size. This does not establish V1 for standard deep networks or unchanged settings. The evaluation split is unspecified.

rows.subject: memory model, 1 head with re-initialization

rows.operation_detail: Trained on randomly labeled data points with key re-initialization enabled.

conditions.value: 100k uniformly generated vectors in R8; 10 uniformly chosen classes

rows.measure: Top-1 validation accuracy on random-label data
rows.note: The authors report near-full convergence qualitatively; an exact accuracy is not stated.

Within the authors' own fitting benchmark, nearly ideal accuracy would count as observed rather than partial, since V1 allows near-zero error; however, training error and the evaluation split are unspecified.
